title: Alnwick Dolphins
text:
Welcome to the Alnwick Dolphins Volunteer Team!
Thank you for volunteering with Alnwick Dolphins.
Our swimming club cannot run without people who are willing to give their time, skills and energy to support swimmers.
Some volunteers will be visible on poolside. Others will work behind the scenes. Some will volunteer every week; others may help at occasional competitions or events.
Every contribution matters.
You do not need to be an experienced swimmer to volunteer.
You do not need to know all the rules.
You do not need to have volunteered before.
What matters is that you are willing to learn, work as part of a team and put the welfare and development of our swimmers at the centre of what you do.
This manual explains how volunteering at Alnwick Dolphins works and provides practical guidance for volunteers.
It should be read alongside the club’s formal policies and procedures.

section: How do I sign up for a role, or find out more?
text:
How do I sign up for a role, or find out more?
You can talk to your swimmer’s coach, or contact us at chair@alnwickdolphins.com. You will receive occasional emails from the club inviting you to sign up for sporadic volunteering opportunities - please do respond to these if you can!
When the club hosts its own events at Willowburn, its all hands on deck! There are lots of volunteering jobs needed to help an event run smoothly. Take a look at the Gala Roles section for some options. When home galas are added to Swim Manager, various Jobs will be available to sign up for via the portal - if you’re unsure, just speak to any member of the coaching squad or committee.

title: 9  Chairperson
text:
9.1 Requirements
The club chair is the principal officer for the club and is elected by the club members.
The chair provides direction and leadership to the club, dealing with issues as and when they arise. They are the ‘face’ of the committee and are intimately involved in all aspects of club organisation. This is a pivotal and highly rewarding role which success and impact on the club will be determined by your own ambitions and enthusiasms. As well as your ability to guide and engage others, it is an opportunity to take on a new challenge and influence the future direction of your club.
Day to day jobs include but are not limited to:
This varied role can (and does!) require a wide range of skills, including good knowledge of the club and competitive swimming, skills in organisation, diplomacy, public speaking and more. The time committment is varied but can be considerable. Its a challenging role but a massively reqarding one.

title: 1  Competition Secretary
text:
1.1 Key Responsibilities
Alnwick Dolphins is a competitive amateur club. We attend a whole range of competitions across the region, and host our own fixtures at Willowburn pool. The competition secretary is responsible for maintaining the competition calendar.
The competition secretary gathers the relevant information, when available, for away events and adds them to Swim Manager, which is the platform that allows swimmers to enter events and pay their fees. This role is also responsible for communicating with the club to advertise upcoming events and to ensure everyone knows the opportunities that exist.
The swimming competition year runs from Autumn to Spring.
Swim England role profile

title: 2  Welfare Officer
text:
2.1 Key Responsibilities
This role is essential in providing a first point of contact for children, parents and adults within the club who have a safeguarding or welfare concern. This person is the advocate for the swimmers, and consequently stays somewhat appart from the Committee and other long term roles. Their responsibility is to act independently and in the best interests of an athlete at the club, putting their needs above that of others and the club itself.

title: 4  Coaches
text:
4.1 Requirements
Swimming coaches are possibly the most important people in the club. Through their expertise, enthusiasm, skills and experience, they get to know all the swimmers in their squads, advocating for each swimmer and helping them achieve their goals.
The coaches ensure they maintain their training to a high standard. They devote a lot of their own time every week to train our swimmers and coordinate a varied, interesting and challenging training schedule that allows everyone to be stretched and challenged.
Coaches are self-organised and punctual, and report to the head coach.

title: 7  Team Manager
text:
We need volunteers to act as team managers for both home and away galas. The Team Manager can be thought of as acting like a teacher taking their class on a school trip.
They ensure that all swimmers are present and correct, get to where they need to be during the event, and act as a point of contact for parents/carers to ensure everybody has all relevant gala information. They play a crucial role in looking after all swimmers, and they take a lead on creating away gala itineraries, organising travel and timings, team kit etc. They should be a person capable of being calm under pressure and maintaining a positive team spirit which ensures our club is viewed positively whereever we go!
Often, the same people volunteer repeatedly to act as team managers, but it is important that we bring in new volunteers to the role, since if we cannot supply a team manager, our swimmers cannot attend away galas.
You will need an up to date DBC check, but no prior experience.
Swim England role profile

title: 19  Code of Conduct
text:
What does being a volunteer mean? Being a volunteer means more than simply giving up your time. When you volunteer for Alnwick Dolphins, you become part of the team representing the club. That means we ask all volunteers to: • act in the best interests of swimmers; • treat everyone with respect; • follow club policies and procedures; • maintain appropriate boundaries; • communicate appropriately; • work cooperatively with coaches and other volunteers; • respect confidentiality; • raise concerns through the appropriate channels; • provide a positive example to swimmers. You are not expected to know everything. You are expected to ask when you are unsure.
Our volunteer principles Everything we do as volunteers should support the club’s values. Passion We want swimmers to enjoy swimming and enjoy being part of Alnwick Dolphins. Belief We encourage swimmers to believe in themselves and their ability to improve. Dedication We recognise the commitment required from swimmers, coaches and volunteers. Respect We treat swimmers, parents, coaches, volunteers, officials and other clubs with respect. Teamwork Swimming may involve individual races, but a successful club is built by people working together.

title: Gala Roles
text:
For galas hosted by Alnwick Dolphins, we need a team of people willing to put time into helping organise and staff the event. On Swim Manager there is the facility to sign up to the different roles for a specific gala - there is no requirement to fulfill that role for more than one gala, or for all days of multi-day galas (but obvioulsy it is easier to manage an event if the volunteers are the same on all days).
You don’t need to be in any other named role to help with a home gala - sign up as you see fit!
The small (but crucial!) volunteer roles that are generally needed and change each time are:

Ticket sales
Raffle stand
Medal table
Runners
Announcer
Team Managers

To host galas, we also need a whole set of Officials of various types - these are really important roles that are essential for hosting our own galas, but they do require a bigger commitment from volunteers. Please have a look at the Officials page for more information.

title: 5  SwimMark Coordinator
text:
This key role involves being the key contact and lead volunteer who manages a swimming club’s SwimMark accreditation process with Swim England.
SwimMark is an accreditation system, renewed every 12 months, which recognises a club is operating in a safe and compliant way and has achieved the minimum standard of safe and effective practice.
Role profile

title: 6  Officials
text:
A British Swimming Official is a voluntary role. To become an Official, you do not need any prior experience, or swimming knowledge. We always need to have new Officials coming through because swims cannot be recorded with Swim England if the right number of each type of Official is present at our events, otherwise the swimmers’ times cannot be used to enter certain competitions.
Each of the following Official roles require a volunteer to commit to undertake (and keep up to date) relevant training and certification. They are listed in order of completion, so you must become a Timekeeper before you can become a Level 1 judge, for example. Which events they volunteer to help at is, however, up to them. Being a registered Official does not mandate you beign available for every event! The more Officials we have, the less each will need to do to cover our home galas.

Timekeepers This is the entry level of roles for swimming officials. It requires you to complete a short course of official training and be at least 14 years old.
Judges Judges are people who have completed the Institute of Swimming training within a time limit of 11 months to receive their judging license (valid for 4 years). There are thee levels of judges. Level 1 is the lowest (entry) level judge. Level 2 judges require to have completed over 20 hours of level 1 judging duties alongside completing additional training. They must be over 15. Level 2S (Starter) is the highest judge level. This is for volunteers who have progressed through levels 1 and 2 and wish to qualify as an official Starter. They need to have completed at least 20 hours of Level 2 judging and additional training.
Starters Once a Level 2 judge has completed a minimum of 20 hours of post qualification experience they are eligible to undertake training to become an official Starter.
Referee A qualified individual (at least 20 years old) who has passed through the training pathway from basic timekeeper to judge to referee. Experience, training and mentoring are required to become a referee. You also need to pass an examination to qualify. If interested in finding out more, see Aquatics GB or speak to a member of the Committee.

title: 8  Marshall
text: Marshalls are responsible for ‘herding’ swimmers on poolside during an event to ensure each swimmer is where they need to be to make sure the gala runs to schedule. It can be hectic, loud and fast-paced poolside, so Marshalls play a key role in bringing some order to the chaos! No prior experience or swimming knowledge is needed to be a gala marshall. You must, however have a basic DBS check and undertake an online child safeguarding course. You can sign up to marshall at one of our events by responding to the link you will be sent via email when a gala is set up on Swim Manager.
